text.description: Perform a team routine with chants or dance, jumps, pyramids or stunts, and tumbling for support or competition. This is more than dance and does not necessarily occur at a sports match.

text.label: Throwing events
text.description: Take part in track-and-field throws: throw a discus, hammer, or javelin, or put the shot.

text.label: Combined events
aliases: Compete in a track-and-field combined event
text.description: Score points across a series of different running, jumping, and throwing events. The whole meet and each attempt may be related but should not be counted twice.

text.label: Jumps
aliases: Do high jump, long jump, or pole vault
text.description: Take part in the high jump, long jump, or pole vault. Specify the event separately.

text.label: Artistic and rhythmic gymnastics
text.description: Practice artistic gymnastics on apparatus or rhythmic gymnastics with apparatus and choreographed routines.

text.label: Sprint
text.description: Run a short distance with maximum acceleration, starting from a position or blocks and aiming to cross the finish as quickly as possible. This is track sprinting, not swimming; swimming has its own “swimming sprint” type.

text.label: Adventure race
aliases: Take part in an adventure race
text.description: Compete in a multidiscipline adventure race by following a route and checkpoints and combining running or trekking, cycling, water, or other stages according to the organizer’s format.

text.label: Outdoor climbing
aliases: Mountaineer or climb on natural terrain
text.description: Climb natural rock or follow a mountaineering route in mountain terrain. A route may include hiking, scrambling or easy climbing, snow or ice, and navigation. Technical roped climbing is one option, not required for every ascent.

text.label: Treadmill or track running
text.description: Run on a stationary treadmill. The movement is still running; the machine’s motor, speed, and incline are equipment or session settings, not a race type.

text.label: Cross-country running
text.description: Run on a cross-country course, field, or varied terrain. Unlike road running, the route usually follows natural ground, though “cross-country” and “trail running” overlap regionally.

text.label: Obstacle course race
aliases: Take part in obstacle course racing
text.description: Run a course while successively clearing organized physical obstacles. Navigation and switching sports are not required, so OCR is not the same as an adventure race.

text.label: Orienteering
text.description: Find designated checkpoints in terrain by choosing a route with a map or compass under competition rules. Running is common, but orienteering is not limited to running.

text.label: Fitness walking
text.description: Walk at a comfortable or brisk pace for physical activity or well-being. This need not be a structured workout and does not define a walk for transportation.

text.label: Parkour
text.description: Move through urban or natural obstacles by running, jumping, climbing over, and landing. Freerunning more often includes showy tricks; specify the style without treating the terms as exact synonyms.

text.label: Sports hike
aliases: Hike as a training or sports session
text.description: Walk a long-distance or hilly route as physical training. A hike without a training focus can remain outdoor recreation; particular route sections or an overnight stay are related phases.

text.label: Power walking
text.description: Walk briskly with purposeful arm movement. No required speed or technique is specified; distinguish this from competitive racewalking.

text.label: Rogaining
text.description: In a team rogaining race, plan a route among checkpoints within a time limit and score points for the checkpoints visited. Unlike ordinary orienteering, it is a long-duration team format with freedom over checkpoint order and value.

text.label: Rucking
aliases: Ruck or walk with a loaded pack
text.description: Walk with a loaded backpack for training or challenge. Carrying a load is a defining difference from an ordinary walk; route and pack weight are session parameters.

text.label: Ultramarathon
text.description: Run an ultrarunning or ultramarathon distance, defined in the cited World Athletics description as longer than a standard 42.195 km marathon. The organizer sets the event’s distance and format; training for an ultra remains a running workout unless the user chooses to track an event.

text.label: Trail running
text.description: Run on natural trails or varied terrain, adjusting your stride to the surface and elevation. Trail running does not require a competition.

text.label: Trekking and summits
aliases: Trek or climb to a summit
text.description: Complete a long-distance or mountain walking route (trekking), or climb toward a specified summit or goal. Route travel and reaching a summit may overlap, but one does not necessarily mean the other.

text.label: Blind football
text.description: Play blind football under a chosen format, usually with an audible ball and agreed communication. Paralympic materials also use the name Football 5-a-side. Outside that context, other five-a-side games may follow different rules and are not automatically blind football.

text.label: Guided running
text.description: Run with a chosen companion or guide runner, using an agreed way to communicate and navigate. The guide is a participation format, not a separate movement or an assumption about diagnosis.

text.label: Boccia
text.description: Play boccia by rolling or throwing leather balls toward the target jack. Under class rules, delivery may be by hand, foot, ramp, or an assistant.

text.label: Goalball
text.description: Roll a ball with bells toward the opposing goal and defend your own line on the court. Hearing the ball and participants’ silence are part of the game.

text.label: Handcycling and para cycling
aliases: Handcycle or take part in para cycling
text.description: This combined label preserves both handcycling (pedaling a bicycle by hand in a handcycle or recumbent hand position) and the broader para-cycling category: adapted cycling or racing on a handcycle, tricycle, tandem with a pilot, or a conventional bicycle in the relevant class. Do not reduce para cycling to handcycles or infer a diagnosis from the equipment.

text.label: Para archery
text.description: Shoot a bow at a target in a chosen para-archery format, using a position or support suited to the participant and discipline rules. Do not infer a class from the equipment.

text.label: Para badminton
text.description: Play badminton in a para class under the chosen rules, moving while standing or using a wheelchair according to the category. The activity is badminton, not a separate mobility method.

text.label: Para canoe
text.description: Paddle a chosen canoe or kayak in a para format to propel the boat. Class and adaptations to the boat or seating are optional or set by the rules.

text.label: Para equestrian
aliases: Take part in para equestrian sport
text.description: Take part in a para equestrian competition or training session by guiding a horse in a chosen discipline, usually para dressage. Class and adaptations describe the participation format.

text.label: Para powerlifting
text.description: Perform a competitive bench press under para powerlifting rules. This para discipline does not imply squats or deadlifts as in powerlifting training.

text.label: Para rowing
text.description: Row in an adapted boat or crew discipline using a suitable body position and equipment. The event, class, and boat are event attributes.

text.label: Para swimming
text.description: Swim or compete in a race under adapted para-swimming classes and rules. Start or assistance method, stroke, and distance are specified by the event, not inferred as a diagnosis.

text.label: Para triathlon
text.description: Complete the swim, cycling, and running or wheelchair legs in a para-triathlon event or workout. Class, equipment, and stages are event parameters.

text.label: Wheelchair racing
text.description: Race in a specialized sports wheelchair by pushing the wheels on a track or road course. Distance and class describe the event, not mobility in general.

text.label: Sitting volleyball
text.description: Play volleyball while seated on the floor, moving the body and arms, blocking, and sending the ball over the net under sitting-volleyball rules.

text.label: Sled hockey
aliases: Play sled hockey or para ice hockey
text.description: Play ice hockey on a sled, using two specialized sticks both to propel and steer and to shoot the puck. Sled hockey is a distinct format, not a synonym for conventional ice hockey.

text.label: Wheelchair badminton
text.description: Play badminton in a wheelchair under the relevant court and classification format, serving and returning the shuttle with a racket. Do not infer a particular class from the activity name.

text.label: Wheelchair basketball
text.description: Play basketball in a sports wheelchair, maneuvering the chair and dribbling, passing, or shooting the ball into the basket. Chair-movement rules are part of the game format.

text.label: Wheelchair curling
text.description: Play wheelchair curling by delivering a stone from a wheelchair toward the house, using a chosen release or assistance method, and strategizing around the stones. Stone delivery and whether sweeping is allowed depend on the format.

text.label: Wheelchair fencing
text.description: Fence with a chosen weapon while seated or secured in a special frame, attacking the valid target and defending under fencing rules. Weapons are foil, épée, or sabre.

text.label: Wheelchair rugby
text.description: Play wheelchair rugby in a specialized chair, advancing or passing the ball toward a scoring zone under this distinct game’s contact rules. This is not conventional rugby.

text.label: Wheelchair tennis
text.description: Rally a tennis ball with a racket while moving in a sports wheelchair. Wheelchair tennis includes an allowed adapted bounce and is not identical to conventional tennis.

text.label: Adaptive yoga and mobility
aliases: Do adapted yoga or mobility practice
text.description: Practice yoga or joint mobility using chosen supports, positions, or ranges of motion. These are two base practices; adaptation describes access and need not be a separate activity type.

text.label: Sit-skiing
text.description: Alpine ski using a sit-ski and chosen assistance or lift access. The access equipment and slope format can be specified separately.

text.label: Adaptive rowing
aliases: Row or paddle with an adaptation
text.description: Row (propel a boat with oars) or paddle (use a bladed paddle) with a chosen adaptation to position, equipment, or assistance. These are different actions but share a user-facing shortcut.

text.label: Seated strength training
text.description: Perform strength exercises while seated with chosen resistance or equipment. “Seated” describes position or access, not a muscle group or diagnosis.

text.label: Adaptive snowboarding
text.description: Ride a snowboard on snow using a chosen adaptation or position. The possibility of adaptation does not mean every participant uses a sit-ski or another specific setup.

text.label: Wheelchair workout
text.description: Train by propelling a manual wheelchair independently: cover a distance, do intervals, or take part in a race.

text.label: Handcycling
aliases: Do handcycling in an adaptive format
text.description: Ride a handcycle. “Adaptive format” describes the equipment or access, not a separate movement activity or an inference about medical status.

text.label: Badminton
text.description: Hit a shuttlecock over a net with a racket, aiming to make it land on the opponent’s court. The shuttle’s flight distinguishes the game from racket sports played with a ball.

text.label: Table tennis
text.description: Rally a lightweight ball across a table net with small rackets. The short rallies and table distinguish table tennis from court tennis.

text.label: Padel
text.description: Play padel on an enclosed court with a racket and ball, using the walls or enclosure as part of rallies under padel rules. Do not confuse it with platform tennis or POP Tennis.

text.label: Pickleball
text.description: Play pickleball with a solid paddle and a hollow perforated ball on a court over a low net. Its equipment and rules distinguish it from padel and platform tennis.

text.label: Platform tennis
aliases: Play platform tennis or paddle tennis
text.description: Play platform tennis on a small raised court with an enclosure, using a solid paddle and a special ball. Another use of the name “paddle tennis” may refer to POP Tennis.

text.label: Beach tennis
text.description: Play beach tennis on a sand court over a net, hitting the ball with a racket before it lands. The surface and rules distinguish it from regular tennis.

text.label: Racquetball
text.description: Hit a rubber ball with a racket against the walls and play out a point in an enclosed court under racquetball rules. Do not use this as a name for squash.

text.label: Real tennis
text.description: Play historic real or court tennis on an asymmetric enclosed court with walls, galleries, and special markings. This is not ordinary tennis or platform tennis.

text.label: Squash
text.description: In an enclosed court, hit a ball with a racket so it rebounds from the front wall. Side and back walls are part of play under squash rules.

text.label: Tennis
text.description: Rally a ball with a racket over a net and within the court boundaries. Singles or doubles, surface, class, and practice are optional details.

text.label: Home physiotherapy
text.description: Perform a prescribed or self-developed set of physiotherapy movements at home. The location does not turn the exercise into household work; prescription and goal are separate details.

text.label: Therapeutic exercise
text.description: Perform a set of graded therapeutic physical exercises under a chosen or prescribed program. Treatment or rehabilitation is context.

text.label: Balance
text.description: Perform controlled tasks for stability, weight transfer, and balance. These may be part of training or rehabilitation.

text.label: Post-injury exercises
text.description: Perform exercises during recovery after an injury. Specify the movement separately; a recovery phase does not imply a particular diagnosis.

text.label: Bodybuilding
text.description: Do strength training to develop muscle size or shape. Hypertrophy is the goal; bodybuilding is a sport or aesthetic practice.

text.label: Station strength circuit
aliases: Do circuit or station-based strength training
text.description: Move through strength-work stations in a circuit with short rests. Exercises may use weights or bodyweight.

text.label: CrossFit
text.description: Perform a workout combining changing strength, gymnastics, and metabolic movements in the style of a chosen functional program. Branded CrossFit and general functional fitness are not exact synonyms.

text.label: Functional training
text.description: Perform strength movements selected for coordination and transfer of effort to everyday or sports activities. A coach’s label alone does not specify a diagnosis or goal.

text.label: Powerlifting
text.description: Train or compete in the squat, bench press, and deadlift under powerlifting rules. Do not conflate it with Olympic weightlifting.

text.label: Barbell, dumbbells and kettlebells
aliases: Lift with a barbell, dumbbells, or kettlebells
text.description: Perform strength sets with weights such as a barbell, dumbbells, or kettlebells. Equipment, exercises, program, and goal are chosen independently.

text.label: Muscular endurance
text.description: Repeat strength efforts or sets with an emphasis on sustaining effort or repeating it many times, rather than only on a single maximal lift.

text.label: Strongman
text.description: Train carrying, lifting, pulling, or holding heavy or unusual objects, or take part in Strongman events. Specify the objects and competition format separately.

text.label: Weight machines
text.description: Perform resistance exercises using strength-training machines. Specify the machine or muscle group as a workout detail.

text.label: Street workout
aliases: Work out at an outdoor calisthenics park
text.description: Do strength or gymnastics exercises on outdoor bars and other available equipment. The park is context, not a separate exercise.

text.label: Core training
text.description: Perform exercises for trunk control and strength endurance. Specific exercises remain components of the session.

text.label: Weightlifting
text.description: Practice the snatch and clean and jerk with a barbell or compete in these Olympic lifts. This differs from powerlifting strength lifts.

text.label: Calisthenics
text.description: Perform strength and control exercises using bodyweight as resistance. Calisthenics may include handstands, pull-ups, and other skills.

text.label: Aquathlon
text.description: Take part in an aquathlon combining running and swimming under the format of the relevant federation. The order and transitions follow the event rules.

text.label: Duathlon
text.description: Complete the running and cycling legs of a duathlon in the specified order. The standard version differs from a triathlon by having no swim leg.

text.label: Mixed workout
aliases: Do a multisport or mixed workout
text.description: Combine several chosen movement or exercise types in one workout. The session determines the components and their order. This is not automatically a competition with a fixed set of stages.

text.label: Multisport race
text.description: Take part in an adventure race as a whole-event, multidiscipline competition. Rules, navigation, and the running, cycling, water, and transition stages depend on the organizer. Preserve the whole event and its activity legs as linked, potentially overlapping and non-additive views.

text.label: Swimrun
text.description: Alternate swimming and running along a route with multiple transitions between land and water. Equipment and stages connect the whole event; an individual run or swim may also be recorded as a leg.

text.label: Triathlon
text.description: Complete successive swim, cycling, and running or wheelchair legs in a triathlon workout or race. The event and its stages may be linked without double-counting time.

text.label: Billiards
text.description: Play a cue sport on a table with a cue and balls. Pool, snooker, and other billiard games have different tables and rules, so specify the variant.

text.label: Bowling
text.description: Approach and roll a ball down a lane to knock over pins. Scoring and repeated frames distinguish bowling from throwing games.

text.label: Darts
text.description: Throw darts at a marked circular target to score or subtract points under the chosen rules. The game mode can be specified separately.

text.label: Disc golf
text.description: Throw a disc from a tee toward a target basket on a course, aiming to complete holes in fewer throws. It shares golf’s course structure, but uses a disc and basket rather than a golf ball and hole.

text.label: Driving range
aliases: Practice golf shots at a driving range
text.description: Practice club swings and ball flight at a driving range. This is range practice, not a round of golf.

text.label: Golf
text.description: Play a round by hitting a ball with clubs from the tee toward each hole, aiming to finish each in as few strokes as possible. Driving-range practice is separate.

text.label: Horseshoes
text.description: Throw horseshoes toward a stake, aiming to ring it or land closer than an opponent. The task is throwing accuracy; the equipment does not make this an equestrian sport.

text.label: Equestrian sport
aliases: Practice equestrian sport, dressage, show jumping, or eventing
text.description: Practice equestrian sport by performing a dressage test, completing a show-jumping course, or taking part in eventing, which combines dressage, cross-country, and show jumping.

text.label: Croquet
text.description: Strike balls with a mallet, guiding them through a sequence of hoops or wickets and toward the finishing peg. Turn order and rules depend on the game variant.

text.label: Pétanque and bocce
text.description: Play a chosen game in the boules family by throwing balls toward a target ball. Pétanque, bocce, and other boules games have their own equipment and rules; specify a local name when useful.

text.label: Shooting sports
text.description: Aim and shoot a sport firearm or air gun at a paper or other target on a shooting range. Specify the discipline or weapon separately; this is not hunting.

text.label: Orienteering
text.description: Find checkpoints with a map or compass and choose their order or route according to the orienteering format. Running, walking, and competition are possible modes, not required by the definition.

text.label: Archery
text.description: Draw a bowstring and release an arrow at a target in a chosen archery discipline. Bow type, distance, target, and indoor or outdoor setting are parameters.

text.label: Shooting and throwing events
aliases: Do target shooting or a throwing event
text.description: Practice target shooting or throw a sports implement for distance or accuracy. Specify the exact discipline separately.

text.label: Horse racing (jockey)
aliases: Compete in a horse race as a jockey
text.description: Race on horseback as a jockey, guiding a horse during a race. This is a mounted race, not spectating or barrel racing.

text.label: Sport fishing
text.description: Cast a line, watch for a bite, and land a fish as a chosen competitive or recreational activity. The type of fishing and its rules are not specified by the label. This is not a target-shooting sport, even though casting takes accuracy.

text.label: BMX freestyle
text.description: Perform BMX trick sequences on ramps, street obstacles, dirt jumps, or a flatland area. The trick or line is the aim, not finishing speed as in BMX racing.

text.label: BMX racing
text.description: Start alongside other BMX racers and ride a short course with hills, rollers, jumps, and turns, competing to finish first. UCI treats this as racing, distinct from BMX freestyle tricks.

text.label: Cyclocross
text.description: Ride repeated laps on a short mixed-surface course of grass, mud, gravel, or obstacles, sometimes dismounting to carry the bike. It differs from road cycling by surface and from mountain biking by course and race format.

text.label: E-MTB
text.description: Ride a mountain bike with electric pedal assist on dirt or mountain trails. MTB route and motor assistance are separate from racing or an ordinary e-bike trip.

text.label: E-bike
text.description: Ride an electric bicycle, pedaling with motor assistance when available. Specify assist level and route separately. The vehicle alone does not say whether the trip is sport, transport, or leisure.

text.label: Hand cycle
text.description: Ride a cycle propelled by hand or hand cranks. Hand propulsion describes the equipment; workout, recreation, transport, and para-cycling race are contexts that should not be inferred from the device.

text.label: Velomobile
text.description: Pedal a velomobile, a multiwheeled or streamlined cycle often ridden in a recumbent position. It is a pedal-powered vehicle, not a car or an ordinary bicycle.

text.label: Gravel riding
text.description: Ride a bicycle on gravel roads and mixed-surface dirt roads or trails. “Gravel” describes a surface or cycling practice, not automatically a race event.

text.label: Indoor trainer and virtual rides
aliases: Ride an indoor trainer or virtual route
text.description: Pedal a bicycle mounted on a home or studio trainer or ergometer, and/or complete a virtual ride using a simulation or digital route. The trainer, indoor session, and virtual format can be combined but need not all apply.

text.label: Mountain biking
aliases: Mountain bike: cross-country, trail, enduro, or downhill
text.description: Ride a mountain bike off-road. This is a user-selected umbrella type that can be refined to XC, trail, enduro, or downhill. XC includes pedaling over varied terrain; trail is riding on trails; enduro uses separately timed climbs or descents as its format specifies; downhill is a fast descent. Do not replace the full practice with only one subtype.

text.label: Road cycling
text.description: Ride a road bicycle mainly on paved roads. A workout, recreational ride, or race is the trip’s goal or format, not the discipline itself.

text.label: Track cycling
text.description: Ride a track bicycle on a banked velodrome for training or a track race. Fixed gearing and banked turns distinguish it from road cycling.

text.label: Bike touring
text.description: Ride a planned bicycle route as a leisure or tourism trip, often with stops or over several days. It does not require racing or sustained training intensity.

text.label: Mountaineering
aliases: Mountaineer or make an alpine ascent
text.description: Follow a high-mountain route, using rock climbing, snow or ice travel, navigation, and rope techniques as needed. Mountaineering covers mountain-route activity more broadly than a single sport-climbing route.

text.label: Bouldering
text.description: Solve short climbing problems on natural rock or a boulder, or on an artificial bouldering wall, usually close to the ground without a rope and with a mat or spotter below. Outdoor and indoor bouldering are different settings of the same discipline; natural rock is included.

text.label: Ice climbing
text.description: Climb a steep ice or mixed route with ice tools and crampons, usually with rope protection. This is not figure skating or speed skating.

text.label: Climbing gym
aliases: Climb at an indoor climbing gym
text.description: Climb a set route on an artificial wall using holds. The format may be ropeless bouldering or roped climbing; specify the chosen route or type separately.

text.label: Rope climbing
text.description: Climb a route with rope protection, using lead or top-rope. Protection mode and route may be sport climbing; bouldering is done close to the ground without a rope.

text.label: Artistic swimming
text.description: Perform a choreographed water routine with figures and coordinated movement solo, in a duet, or as a team. “Synchronized swimming” is an older or colloquial name for artistic swimming, not a separate discipline.

text.label: Bodyboarding
text.description: Catch a wave and ride it prone or on the knees on a short, buoyant bodyboard. This differs from stand-up surfing and from skimboarding near shore.

text.label: Canoe sprint and slalom
text.description: Paddle a canoe in a sport session or race. Specify either sprint over a marked distance or slalom through gates or a course, as these are different tasks.

text.label: Scuba diving
text.description: Dive underwater with a self-contained breathing apparatus (tank and regulator) to explore or complete an underwater segment. This differs from surface snorkeling and breath-hold diving.

text.label: Freediving
text.description: Practice diving or apnea without a self-contained tank. This may be static breath-holding at the surface, dynamic underwater swimming on a breath hold, or a depth dive; freediving is not limited to deep dives.

text.label: Rowing
aliases: Row on water or an indoor rowing machine
text.description: Row a boat on the water or perform a rowing stroke cycle on an indoor ergometer. The first is water rowing; the second is training on a stationary machine.

text.label: Kitesurfing
text.description: Ride a board on water while holding and steering an airborne kite that pulls the rider. This differs from windsurfing, where a sail is attached to the board by a mast.

text.label: Kayaking
text.description: Paddle and steer a kayak or canoe in a chosen water or leisure format. Hull or paddle type, calm, sea, or white water, and racing are separate details.

text.label: Longboard surfing
text.description: Ride an ocean or artificial wave on a long surfboard. The longer board allows characteristic smooth turns and cross-steps; this is a type of wave surfing, not land-based longboarding.

text.label: Marathon swimming
text.description: Swim a long distance in an organized open-water race or workout. The event sets the exact distance and rules; this is a long-duration open-water format, not a separate stroke.

text.label: Sailing
aliases: Sail or take part in a sailing regatta
text.description: Operate a sailboat during a training or recreational session. A regatta is an event or competition format, not a synonym for all sailing.

text.label: Open water swimming
text.description: Swim in natural open water, such as a lake, sea, or river, without a pool lane. Temperature, current, route, and environmental safety distinguish the session from pool swimming.

text.label: Wellness swimming
aliases: Swim for rehabilitation or do aquatic fitness
text.description: Swim or exercise in water for rehabilitation, or do aquatic fitness. Specify the exercises and recovery goal separately if useful.

text.label: Pool swimming
text.description: Swim through pool water using a chosen stroke or pace. Lanes, lengths, and workout plan are parameters; play or rehabilitation goals may be separate simultaneous meanings.

text.label: Apnea
aliases: Spearfish or practice apnea as a physical activity
text.description: This combined category preserves two practices: (1) spearfishing—search for or take fish or another resource underwater using a chosen permitted method; breathing equipment depends on method and location; and (2) freediving or apnea—practice static breath-holding, dynamic underwater swimming on a breath hold, or diving without a self-contained tank, not necessarily to hunt. Do not reduce the whole label to only one of these two parts.

text.label: Boating
aliases: Go boating near shore for recreation
text.description: Travel in a small boat along the shore for leisure as a rower or passenger. Specify whether you operate the boat and how it moves—oar, motor, or sail—separately.

text.label: Diving
text.description: Jump or dive into water from a springboard or platform and perform aerial or rotational elements before entry. This is diving as a jumping discipline, not scuba diving.

text.label: Rafting
text.description: Paddle as a team in an inflatable raft through rapids or fast-flowing water, steering the craft along a river route. Being a passenger on a calm-water trip is a different mode.

text.label: Surfing
text.description: Paddle into a wave and then ride across its surface while standing or maneuvering on a surfboard. Board type, wave, and sport or leisure format are attributes.

text.label: Skimboarding
text.description: Run along the shore and toss a flat board onto a thin layer of water or wet sand, then jump on and glide toward a breaking shore wave or perform flatland tricks. In wave skimboarding the rider actually rides the wave; starting from shore or shallow water distinguishes it from paddling out in deeper water for conventional surfing.

text.label: Snorkeling
text.description: Swim or float near the surface wearing a mask and snorkel, breathing air above the water while observing underwater life. Brief dives may occur, but repeated breath-holds or depth practice are freediving.

text.label: Stand-up paddleboarding
text.description: Stand on a board and paddle with a long paddle to move across the water. SUP may be leisure paddling, surfing, racing, or fitness; the board is equipment.

text.label: Wakeboarding
text.description: Ride a wakeboard while holding a tow rope and being pulled by a boat or cable system. The pull is external, unlike self-propelled sailing or kitesurfing.

text.label: Windsurfing
text.description: Glide across water on a board while steering a sail attached to a mast. Steering with a sail distinguishes windsurfing from kiteboarding, which uses a separate towing kite.

text.label: Water skiing
text.description: Glide across water on one or two water skis while holding a tow handle attached to a boat or cable. Do not confuse this with snow skiing.

text.label: Splitboarding
text.description: Tour uphill in splitboard mode, with the board divided into skis, then reassemble it for an off-piste descent. The equipment and uphill access differ from an ordinary snowboard ride.

text.label: Classic cross-country skiing
text.description: Travel on cross-country skis using classic technique where permitted: diagonal stride, double-pole or alternating poling, kick-double-poling, and other allowed classic variations. Unlike free or skate style, it does not use sideways ski push-offs as in skating.

text.label: Figure skating
text.description: Perform figures, steps, spins, and jumps on ice in a practice or artistic program on skates. This differs from recreational skating and speed skating.

text.label: Freeride skiing
text.description: Ski off a prepared or marked piste on natural snow. Freeride and backcountry overlap, but backcountry may imply remote terrain, traveling in independently, and separate avalanche preparation.

text.label: Alpine skiing
text.description: Descend a snowy slope on alpine skis, turning and controlling speed. A groomed run, lift, freeride, or race is context or a subtype.

text.label: Ice rink
aliases: Recreational ice skate at a rink
text.description: Glide on skates around a rink for leisure. If the session consists of figure-skating elements, speed racing, or hockey, choose that more specific type.

text.label: Sledding and tubing
aliases: Sled or tube down a hill
text.description: Slide down a snowy or icy slope on a sled or an inflatable inner tube. Tubing and steerable sleds use different equipment, but both are recreational descents, not skiing.

text.label: Curling
text.description: Push a heavy stone over ice toward the target (“house”) and control its path or speed with sweeping under curling rules. This is not an ordinary throw or glide.

text.label: Ice hockey
text.description: Play ice hockey on an ice rink or arena, skating and controlling a flat puck with a stick. The game includes skating, passing, and shooting. “On ice” and “with a puck” are clarifying names for the same ordinary form of hockey.

text.label: Skate skiing
text.description: Glide on cross-country skis by pushing alternately sideways in a V-shaped skating stride, usually on a wide prepared track. This is not classic stride in a ski groove.

text.label: Ski touring
text.description: Ascend and descend a snowy mountain route on skis using uphill mode, such as skins, free heel, or a climbing binding. Ski mountaineering adds technical mountain travel or mountaineering sections; both scopes are kept in this combined label until a finer split is wanted.

text.label: Speed skating
text.description: Accelerate and complete a lap or distance on skates to achieve a time or placing. Racing line and strategy distinguish it from figure skating.

text.label: Snowshoeing
text.description: Walk over loose or deep snow in snowshoes that distribute weight and reduce sinking. A winter walk without snowshoes and skiing are different ways to travel.

text.label: Snowboarding
text.description: Descend a snowy slope on a single snowboard, steering with its edges. A regular slope run does not imply park jumps or backcountry.

text.label: Snowkiting
text.description: Travel on snow on skis or a snowboard using the pull of a steerable kite. This is not kitesurfing on water, though the pulling equipment is similar.

text.label: Winter trekking
text.description: Walk a winter route on snow or ice. Boots, poles, or snowshoes may help, but the activity differs from skiing uphill or technical mountaineering.

text.label: Guided excursion
aliases: Take a guided tour or walk
text.description: Walk or travel with a guide, following a route and listening to or viewing its points of interest. The place and mode of travel are context.

text.label: City walk
text.description: Take an unhurried walk along a city street or waterfront for leisure, observing the city and its life. If the goal is to get somewhere, it may be walking for transportation.

text.label: Boat trip
aliases: Take a coastal boat ride or boat tour
text.description: Be a passenger or guest on a leisure boat trip at sea or on another body of water to relax and enjoy the scenery. Operating a sailboat or rowing are separate activities.

text.label: Weekend trip
text.description: Make a short leisure trip or excursion out of town or to a new place. The trip is the overall event; driving, walking a route, and sightseeing may be separate layers.

text.label: Relaxing by the water
text.description: Spend time relaxing by the sea, river, or lake, without necessarily swimming or using a boat. Swimming or bathing may overlap in time but has its own tag.

text.label: Picnic
text.description: Spend time relaxing and sharing food outdoors, usually seated at a chosen spot. Preparing food or traveling there may be separate concurrent activities.

text.label: Beach
aliases: Spend leisure time at the beach, sunbathe, or swim
text.description: Enjoy a beach outing by lying down or sunbathing, playing, or swimming without a set sport distance. Training swims and surfing are specified separately.

text.label: Park
text.description: Spend time in an urban or nature park for relaxation and free-time activities. Visiting the place does not specify whether the person sits, walks, or exercises.

text.label: Viewpoint
aliases: Visit a viewpoint or natural landmark
text.description: Arrive at a viewpoint or natural attraction and look at the view or feature. The climb, hike, or trip there is a related but separate stage.

text.label: Sitting outdoors
aliases: Sit or rest outdoors, perhaps in a hammock
text.description: Spend time sitting or lying outdoors to rest or take in the surroundings. A hammock is one possible means of relaxing, not required or defining the whole activity.

text.label: By the campfire
text.description: Spend time near a campfire talking, watching the fire, or relaxing. Lighting or tending the fire is a separate practical task.

text.label: Aimless walk
text.description: Walk for rest, experiences, or conversation, rather than to reach another required destination. Route, duration, and setting can be recorded separately.

text.label: Waterfront walk
aliases: Walk along a waterfront or through a park
text.description: Walk through a park or along a waterfront for a stroll or relaxation. Green space or water describes the setting, not a separate sport.

text.label: Dog walk
text.description: Walk a dog along a street or through a park. Pace and route can be flexible; feeding and caring for the pet are separate chores.

text.label: Road trip
aliases: Take a road trip or scenic drive
text.description: Drive a chosen scenic route for the journey and views, often stopping along the way. A trip to a required destination may instead be ordinary transportation.

text.label: Safari
aliases: Take a safari or wildlife tour
text.description: Join an organized outing to observe wild animals on foot, by boat, or by vehicle. This is guided wildlife viewing, not independent species searching or hunting.

text.label: Enjoying the scenery
text.description: Observe a landscape for aesthetic enjoyment, without requiring a walk, guided tour, or photography.

text.label: Sightseeing
text.description: Visit city attractions as a tourist, moving between places and choosing points of interest. This is broader than one guided walk, which may be a separate format.

text.label: Birdwatching
text.description: Find and observe birds in their natural environment, noting species and behavior through visual, auditory, and other field signs. Visual searching and birding by ear are possible methods or subtypes, not the only meaning of birding.

text.label: Botanical walk
text.description: Walk with a focus on plants, plant communities, and the natural environment, observing or identifying species. An ordinary walk may happen at the same time.

text.label: Photos on a walk
text.description: Take purposeful photographs while also walking. Photography and walking may both be retained as meanings of one event that does not overlap itself in time.

text.label: Wildlife photography and tracking
text.description: Photograph wild animals and/or read signs or tracks of their presence, without taking the animal. Wildlife photography and tracking are distinct but can be combined observation methods.

text.label: Geocaching
text.description: Search for a hidden physical container or object using GPS coordinates or a clue, then log the find under geocaching rules. The route to the location is part of the game, but driving is not required.

text.label: Urban nature
text.description: Notice and explore wildlife in an urban setting, including birds, plants, insects, and ecosystems, often including human-shaped places. This is not just a city walk.

text.label: Species survey
aliases: Do citizen science or a species survey
text.description: Take part in a project field survey under its protocol: find or observe organisms and submit a record usable for science. Later labeling or validation may be a separate online session.

text.label: Tracks and local nature lore
aliases: Interpret tracks or study local natural history
text.description: Explore a local natural area by identifying tracks, geological or ecological signs, and their context. Reading a guidebook without observing the site is a different format.

text.label: Mushroom foraging
text.description: Look for and gather mushrooms in a natural area. Gathering may include checking edibility, but the purpose and local rules are not specified by the label.

text.label: Genealogy
text.description: Collect, verify, and connect documents, records, and testimony about family history. Visiting an archive, reading a document, and transcribing it may be separate research steps.

text.label: Letterboxing
text.description: Find a hidden box using written clues or a route, locate its stamp, and leave a mark in the logbook. Unlike geocaching, the search is usually not based on GPS coordinates.

text.label: Meteor shower
text.description: Watch the sky during a meteor shower and note visible meteors. A planetarium or recorded video is not field observation.

text.label: Wildlife
text.description: Watch animals living freely in the wild, aiming not to interfere. An organized safari or observing animals at a zoo has a different context.

text.label: Insects
text.description: Search for, observe, and identify insects in nature, often by shape or behavior. Catching or collecting them is not implied.

text.label: Weather
text.description: Observe local weather conditions directly, including clouds, precipitation, wind, and changes. Scientific recording of measurements may be an additional activity.

text.label: Birding by ear
text.description: Find or identify birds mainly by their calls and other field sounds, listening to the surrounding environment. Recordings or audio recognition at home are different from observing birds in the field.

text.label: Stargazing and astronomy
aliases: Observe the stars or practice astronomy
text.description: Observe celestial objects and phenomena in the day or night sky with the unaided eye or an instrument. Reading about astronomy or working with data indoors is a different mode.

text.label: Urbex
aliases: Explore unusual or abandoned urban sites (urbex)
text.description: Explore unusual or abandoned urban architecture and infrastructure from outside or with authorized access, observing and documenting it. Dangerous or unauthorized entry is not implied.

text.label: Plant identification
text.description: Examine a plant and identify its species or family from observable features or a key. Collecting the plant is not implied.

text.label: Scavenger hunt
aliases: Do a scavenger hunt or clue-based quest
text.description: Search for a list of real objects or clues and confirm what you find. This is broader than the specific rules of geocaching or letterboxing.

text.label: Plein air
aliases: Draw or photograph outdoors on site
text.description: Draw or photograph on location while directly observing a subject or landscape in the field. The method may be drawing or using a camera; a trip or walk may be an additional meaning.

text.label: Rockhounding and fossils
aliases: Search for minerals, rocks, and fossils
text.description: Search for and examine geological specimens or fossils, and collect them when permitted, as a collecting activity. Industrial extraction and collecting in protected areas are not implied.

text.label: Wild berries and plants
text.description: Gather wild berries or plants for personal use in a place where it is permitted. Identifying species or taking a walk may accompany the gathering but is not synonymous with it.

text.label: Tide pools
text.description: At low tide, examine pools in the intertidal zone and observe their organisms and surroundings. Collecting organisms is not required.

text.label: Backpacking
text.description: Travel on a multi-day walking route with a carried backpack and overnight stops along the way. This integrated trekking format differs from car camping at a base.

text.label: Bivouac
text.description: Spend the night in a minimal, temporary camp directly along a route or in the open. It is a simple, short-term stop rather than an equipped campground.

text.label: Car camping
text.description: Stay in a tent or with camping gear beside a car or at a campsite, bringing the gear by vehicle. Backpacking on foot is not implied.

text.label: Campsite holiday
aliases: Take a caravan or camping holiday
text.description: Spend a holiday with overnight stays in a caravan, camper, or at campsites, moving between pitches. The lodging format does not mean driving for the entire period.

text.label: Glamping
text.description: Stay outdoors in pre-equipped, comfortable accommodation such as a tent or cabin. This is a lodging style, not a walking trek or pitching your own tent.

text.label: Motorhome
aliases: Stay in a motorhome or RV
text.description: Travel or stay overnight in a motorhome or RV and use its living facilities. Driving and resting at a campsite are distinct activities.

text.label: Tent camping
text.description: Pitch a tent and spend time outdoors, including overnight. Camping is a lodging or trip format; hiking, cooking, and sleeping may be separate segments.

text.label: Sledding and tubing
aliases: Ride an inflatable tube for fun
text.description: Ride an inflatable tube for play or recreation, sliding down a snowy slope or floating on water, such as a river or a towed water tube. The setting and propulsion vary; this is not limited to snow tubing.

text.label: Boating
text.description: Ride in a pleasure boat as a passenger or operate one for recreational boating. Rowing, sailing, and motor navigation are different ways to take part.

text.label: Leisure kayak or SUP
aliases: Take a leisure outing by kayak or SUP
text.description: Paddle a kayak or canoe, or stand on a SUP board, for a relaxed outing on the water. Kayaking and SUP use different equipment and postures; racing, surfing, and workout sessions are different modes.

text.label: Recreational hunting
aliases: Hunt or shoot outdoors for recreation (personal choice)
text.description: Take part in recreational hunting or shooting in a natural setting as permitted by local rules; searching, stalking, and shooting are distinct methods. This is not wildlife observation, and the activity is not presumed harmless or unlawful.

text.label: Leisure sailing
text.description: Operate a sailboat or yacht, or take part in a recreational outing under sail, using the wind for propulsion. An official race or regatta is a different competitive context.

text.label: Kite flying
text.description: Launch, hold, and steer a kite in an open area. A picnic may be a concurrent setting; making the kite is a separate maker project.

text.label: Horseback ride
aliases: Go for a relaxed horseback ride
text.description: Ride a horse at a relaxed pace along a chosen route and enjoy the outing. A riding lesson, working with the horse, or a competition may be separate contexts.

text.label: Rod fishing
text.description: Cast or lower fishing gear, watch for a bite, and bring in fish as part of recreational fishing. The type of fishing, catch-and-release, or keeping a catch can be specified as context or a variant.

text.label: Snorkeling to watch sea life
text.description: Swim near the surface with a mask and snorkel while observing underwater life. Brief dives may occur, but scuba with a tank and athletic apnea or freediving involve different breathing methods or exertion.

text.label: Via ferrata
text.description: Climb a protected rock route using a continuous steel safety cable, carabiners, and steps for progress. It is a protected hiking route rather than an ordinary rock-climbing route, but requires specialized equipment and skills.

text.label: Night birding by ear
aliases: Do acoustic birding or count night migrants
text.description: Listen for and identify birds by their calls or songs in the field (acoustic birding). This can also include the narrower, separate practice of recording or counting nocturnal flight calls from migrating birds; acoustic birding as a whole is not limited to night migration.

text.label: Environmental monitoring
text.description: Repeatedly measure or record selected geological or ecological indicators at a site to track changes over time. A one-off visit without a series of observations is not necessarily monitoring.

text.label: BioBlitz
aliases: Run or take part in a BioBlitz
text.description: Organize or join a time-limited, intensive BioBlitz: observe and record as many species as possible at a chosen site. This is an event or project, not a single identification technique.

text.label: Bird checklist
text.description: Record observed bird species in an ongoing list or checklist, noting place and date and optionally the number of individuals. Searching for birds is a preceding or concurrent activity.

text.label: Weather observations for a project
aliases: Record weather observations for a project
text.description: Regularly observe and enter weather measurements for a citizen-science project using its protocol. Simply noticing rain or checking a forecast is not project monitoring.

text.label: Logging an observation
aliases: Record an observation, with species, media, or conditions
text.description: Document a field finding: species or trait, place and time, and, when needed, a photo, audio, or description of conditions. Recording it is not the same as later verifying the identification.

text.label: Verifying IDs
aliases: Add or check a taxonomic label
text.description: Add or check the taxonomic label (organism name or group) on an observation using available features or identification keys. A comment or confirming the record may be separate steps.

text.label: Identifying others’ sightings
text.description: Review a photo or record already uploaded by another participant and suggest a species or taxonomic identification. This is online community validation, not your own field encounter.

text.label: Tagging photos and sounds
aliases: Label images or audio for a citizen-science project
Label audio data for a citizen-science project
text.description: Annotate images or audio recordings according to a project protocol by marking objects, features, sounds, or time intervals. This does not involve collecting new recordings in the field.

text.label: Checking observation quality
aliases: Check an observation’s quality, location, or date
text.description: Review a user-submitted field record for completeness and plausible coordinates, date, and metadata without replacing its taxonomic identification.

text.label: Transcribing archives
aliases: Transcribe a historical document or archive record
text.description: Transfer a handwritten or scanned historical source into editable text, preserving the words that can be read and marking illegible passages. This is crowdsourced archival work, not passive reading.

text.label: Meditation
text.description: Practice a chosen meditation or mindfulness technique. A particular goal or tradition is optional; simply resting without doing anything can be recorded differently.

text.label: Doing nothing
text.description: Spend time in quiet rest without an intentional external task. Sleep and screen-based content are separate chosen activities.

text.label: Daydreaming and reflection
aliases: Reflect, observe your thoughts, daydream, or contemplate
text.description: Think things over, consider a question, daydream, or observe your thoughts and surroundings. This may be deliberate or free-form. Formal meditation is a possible separate personal practice, not a required distinction.

text.label: Browsing shops without buying
aliases: Browse shop windows without planning a purchase
Browse shops without planning a purchase
text.description: Take your time looking at shops or their windows without a specific purchase in mind. Purposeful shopping or completing a purchase can be recorded separately.

text.label: Delivery
aliases: Deliver orders and freight as work
Deliver orders, materials, mail, or goods as work
text.description: Transport orders, materials, mail, or goods as part of a job.

text.label: Driving for work
aliases: Drive or operate a vehicle professionally
text.description: Professionally operate a vehicle or machine; this does not mean riding as a passenger.

text.label: Professional cleaning
aliases: Clean or service a facility professionally
Clean or maintain a facility for work
text.description: Professionally clean or maintain a building, site, or facility.

text.label: Building operations
text.description: Carry out building or facility operations and related operational work.

text.label: Loading and unloading
text.description: Load or unload cargo, or move it from place to place.

text.label: Order picking
text.description: Gather items for an order, assemble or kit them, and pack them.

text.label: Receiving goods
aliases: Receive, check, and put away stock
text.description: Accept a delivery or goods, check them against the shipment, and put them in their assigned place.

text.label: Dispatching
aliases: Route and dispatch orders or vehicles
text.description: Plan or assign routes and dispatch an order or vehicle.

text.label: Preparing a shipment
aliases: Prepare a shipment and hand it to a carrier
text.description: Prepare the shipment and its paperwork, then transfer it to the carrier.

text.label: Stock and replenishment
text.description: Put stock in place, replenish it, and maintain inventory.

text.label: Traffic and access control
aliases: Control traffic, access, or a safety zone
text.description: Manage movement, access, or the boundaries of a safe work zone.

text.label: Vehicle inspection
aliases: Inspect a vehicle or machine before a shift or handoff
text.description: Inspect a vehicle or piece of equipment before a shift or when handing it over.

text.label: Work vehicle repair
aliases: Service or repair a work vehicle
text.description: Maintain or repair a vehicle used professionally.

text.label: Waste and recycling
aliases: Collect, sort, or process waste and recyclables
text.description: Collect, sort, or process waste or recyclable materials.

text.label: Returns and defects
aliases: Sort, inspect, or route returns and defective goods
text.description: Sort, inspect, or route returned or defective goods. Map specific repair or repacking to the matching canonical activity when tracked separately.

text.label: Sorting goods
aliases: Sort, label, or assign goods by use or quality
Sort or label goods by quality
text.description: Sort or label materials or goods, or assign them by intended use or quality.

text.label: Setting up for a specialist
aliases: Stage tools, materials, or a workspace for another worker
text.description: Provide or prepare tools, materials, and a work area for another person carrying out a task.

text.label: Ship power systems
aliases: Monitor a ship’s power systems or equipment
text.description: Monitor the indicators or equipment of a vessel’s power system.

text.label: Ship watch
text.description: Stand watch or monitor the operation of a vessel.

text.label: Scrolling a feed
aliases: Browse a feed or other media
text.description: Browse a feed, websites, or a collection of material, moving from one post or item to another.

text.label: Audio and podcasts
aliases: Listen to audio or a podcast
text.description: Listen to a podcast, recording, broadcast, or other material that is primarily spoken.

text.label: Music
text.description: Choose to listen to recorded or streamed music as an activity.

text.label: Movie or series
text.description: Watch a film, series, or individual episode.

text.label: Video
text.description: Watch video clips, programs, or streams without specifying a film or series.

text.label: Military service
aliases: Carry out a military service duty
text.description: Record carrying out an assigned military, service, or operational duty at a neutral level. Service profile is recorded through `axis.role` or `axis.discipline`; use general nodes for specific observed work such as command, training, logistics, monitoring, or maintenance. The label does not reveal tactics, use-of-force methods, or restricted information.

text.label: Trip to a meeting or event
aliases: Travel to a social, community, or spiritual event
text.description: Travel by vehicle or on foot to a social gathering, community event, or spiritual practice. Waiting along the way may be part of the route.

text.label: Commute
text.description: Travel by any means to or from work or a place of study.

text.label: Errand trip
aliases: Trip to a repair or service provider
text.description: Travel, walk, transport goods, or accompany someone for a household errand.

text.label: Transport for own farm
aliases: Travel or transport for own-use production
text.description: Travel, walk, transport goods, or accompany people as part of own-use production.

text.label: Trip to a service
aliases: Travel for personal care or a service
text.description: Travel or walk, and wait along the route, for personal care or a service for yourself.

text.label: Other trip
text.description: Travel to a chosen destination for an errand or as part of a journey.

text.label: Waiting while traveling
text.description: Wait for transport, a connection, or the next part of a journey.

text.label: Walking somewhere
text.description: Walk in order to reach a chosen place.

text.label: Cardio
text.description: Exercise with the primary goal of developing endurance.

text.label: Training hike
text.description: Walk a route as training or deliberate physical exertion.

text.label: Mobility and stretching
text.description: Do exercises for joint mobility, flexibility, and stretching.

text.label: Sport practice
text.description: Train or take part in a chosen sport by practicing its movements, techniques, and game actions.

text.label: Strength training
text.description: Exercise with resistance, weights, or body weight to develop strength.

text.label: 3D printing parts
text.description: Prepare and carry out 3D printing or post-process a part.

text.label: Line assembly
aliases: Assemble a product at a station or line
text.description: Assemble a product at a workstation or on a production line.

text.label: Bookbinding and print finishing
text.description: Bind, fold, trim, or otherwise finish printed materials from a production run.

text.label: Quality control
aliases: Check a product against quality standards
text.description: Inspect a product, its parameters, or its dimensions against a standard.

text.label: Tooling maintenance
text.description: Maintain workshop tools, production tooling, or fixtures.

text.label: Process control
aliases: Monitor a production line and correct deviations
Monitor process parameters and correct deviations
text.description: Monitor the process or its parameters and address deviations.

text.label: Machine operation
aliases: Operate a production machine or line
text.description: Operate a machine, piece of equipment, or production line to manufacture goods.

text.label: Packing and labeling
text.description: Pack or label finished products.

text.label: Equipment setup
aliases: Prepare equipment for a production run
Prepare or change over a machine for a batch
text.description: Prepare or reconfigure a machine or workstation for a production batch.

text.label: Prepress
aliases: Prepare files and forms for print production
Prepare materials and plates for a print run
text.description: Prepare text, layout, or printing plates for a print run, including prepress checks. This is separate from designing the original, running the press, or binding the finished work when tracked as separate segments.

text.label: Food production
text.description: Process food raw materials into products for storage or sale. Distinguish this from preparing and serving food for immediate consumption or a guest.

text.label: Machining parts
aliases: Process materials or components for manufacturing
text.description: Process a material or component using a manufacturing method.

text.label: Machine programming
aliases: Set up numerical controls for production
text.description: Configure digital or numerical controls for a manufacturing operation.

text.label: Batch records
aliases: Record a production run, batch, or result
text.description: Create a production record for a run, batch, or result.

text.label: Fixing defects
aliases: Rework an item that failed inspection
text.description: Rework an item that did not pass quality control.

text.label: Print runs
text.description: Print a production run of printed materials. This excludes creating the graphic original or preparing materials for printing when those are separate segments.

text.label: Garment manufacturing
text.description: Sew garments, soft goods, or textile products. Designing clothing and repairing an existing item are related but distinct actions.

text.label: Product testing
text.description: Test a product after assembly.

text.label: Weaving and knitting
text.description: Produce textile fabric by interlacing or knitting yarns. The specific material can be recorded on the material axis.

text.label: Acrobatic gymnastics
text.description: Perform paired or group gymnastics balances, lifts, throws, catches, and acrobatic elements as part of a joint routine.

text.label: Aerobic gymnastics
text.description: Perform an aerobic gymnastics routine combining aerobic movement with strength, dynamic, jumping, and flexibility elements. Individual, pair, or group composition depends on the format.

text.label: Air rifle shooting
aliases: Shoot an air rifle at a target
text.description: Take part in target shooting with an air rifle in the Target Sprint discipline.

text.label: Natural track luge
text.description: Ride a sled down a natural ice track, steering to control direction and speed. The format and track conditions vary by event.

text.label: Krabi krabong
text.description: Practice krabi krabong through martial exercises and forms using traditional Thai swords and a staff or pole.

text.label: Muay Talay
text.description: Compete in Muay Talay by balancing and trying to knock an opponent off a narrow beam or log under the rules of the event.

text.label: Wai Kru
text.description: Perform Wai Kru, a ritualized dance ceremony associated with Muay Thai. Taking part in a contest or demonstration of the ceremony differs from sparring.

text.label: Sanda
text.description: Practice Sanda wushu in contact bouts, using permitted hand and foot strikes and throws under Sanda rules.

text.label: Water ski show
text.description: Take part in show skiing by performing water-ski tricks and synchronized group figures in a staged performance.

text.label: Finswimming
text.description: Swim using a monofin or two fins, propelling yourself by muscular effort at the surface or underwater.

text.label: Underwater hockey
text.description: Play at the bottom of a pool: use a short stick to move a puck and score in the opposing team’s goal while swimming with a mask, snorkel, and fins.

text.label: Underwater rugby
text.description: Play a contact team game underwater: hold and pass a ball and place it in a basket-shaped goal on the pool bottom, using a mask, snorkel, and fins.

text.label: Underwater orienteering
text.description: Navigate underwater using a compass and distance measurements, find or pass control points, and complete a set course while remaining submerged.

text.label: Underwater target shooting
text.description: Shoot at a target underwater with a speargun or harpoon while holding your breath. The event scores hits and, in some formats, speed moving between targets.

text.label: Mermaiding
text.description: Swim and perform movement or expressive elements at the surface and underwater while wearing a mermaid tail with a monofin.

text.label: Underwater wrestling
text.description: Wrestle one-on-one in and under the water, trying to remove a ribbon from the opponent’s ankle and show it above the water.

text.label: Bike orienteering
text.description: Ride a mountain bike between control points, using a map and route and choosing a path between points.

text.label: Ski orienteering
text.description: Use cross-country skis to navigate by map and pass control points along a chosen route.

text.label: Trail-O
text.description: In Trail-O, determine from a control station which marker corresponds to the control point shown on the map, following the event’s accuracy or timing rules.

text.label: Field lacrosse
text.description: Play field lacrosse by catching, passing, and throwing a ball with a stick on an outdoor field.

text.label: Lacrosse sixes
text.description: Play lacrosse Sixes, a compact, fast-paced format with six players and its own rules.

text.label: Kickboxing musical forms
text.description: Perform choreographed individual or group kickboxing movements and techniques to music, without sparring.

text.label: Karate kata
text.description: Perform kata in karate: a prescribed sequence of offensive and defensive techniques in a set order and direction.

text.label: Kumite
text.description: Compete in kumite by sparring with a karate opponent and scoring with permitted techniques under WKF rules.

text.label: Guts
aliases: Play Guts with a flying disc
text.description: Play Guts by throwing a disc at the opposing team, whose players try to catch it in the target zone.

text.label: Disc freestyle
text.description: Perform individual or paired trick combinations using a flying disc, with throws and catches.

text.label: Double Disc Court
text.description: Play Double Disc Court (DDC): two teams throw two discs at the other side at the same time under DDC rules.

text.label: Discathon
text.description: Run a course while throwing a disc toward checkpoints or the finish in Discathon.

text.label: Disc throwing
aliases: Practice accuracy or distance disc throwing
text.description: Practice throwing a flying disc for accuracy or distance. The specific exercise can be recorded separately.

text.label: Self-caught flight
text.description: Throw a disc, run or position yourself under its flight, and catch it while recording time or distance in MTA/TRC.

text.label: Goaltimate
text.description: Play Goaltimate, a team flying-disc game with goals or a hoop and its own rules.

text.label: Discflect
text.description: Play Discflect, a team flying-disc game with a target zone and its own rules.

text.label: Disco
text.description: Perform choreographed combinations in a disco style to the rhythm of the music, in practice or competition.

text.label: Merengue
text.description: Dance merengue using its characteristic partnered or solo step pattern to merengue music.

text.label: American smooth
text.description: Perform selected American Smooth ballroom dances, with characteristic travel across the floor and partner leading.

text.label: American rhythm
text.description: Perform selected American Rhythm ballroom dances with a partner, using their characteristic rhythms and technique.

text.label: Acrobatic rock and roll
text.description: Dance acrobatic rock and roll as a pair, performing fast rock-and-roll steps, jumps, and supported acrobatic elements.

text.label: Boogie-woogie
text.description: Dance Boogie Woogie, a partnered swing dance with characteristic rhythm and steps and competitive improvisation.

text.label: Bugg
text.description: Dance Bugg, a partnered swing dance with characteristic steps and figures under Bugg rules.

text.label: Carom billiards
text.description: Play carom billiards by striking your cue ball so that it contacts both object balls, under carom rules.

text.label: English billiards
text.description: Play English billiards by using a cue to strike the white and object balls and score under English billiards rules.

text.label: Rally
aliases: Compete in a rally car race
text.description: Compete in an automobile rally by completing timed special stages and the connecting routes under rally rules.

text.label: Rally raid and off-road racing
aliases: Compete in an off-road car race or rally raid
text.description: Compete in an off-road automobile race or rally raid, driving a challenging navigation course or special stages under FIA competition rules.

text.label: Gliding
text.description: Pilot an unpowered aircraft and use rising air currents to gain altitude and travel along a route.

text.label: Aerobatics
aliases: Perform aerobatics in an airplane or glider
text.description: Perform aerobatic maneuvers in an airplane or glider, completing a sequence of figures in a defined airspace.

text.label: Aeromodelling
text.description: Take part in the aeromodelling family of activities. Building a model and operating it in flight are distinct activities and may be timed separately, or the user may record the full aeromodelling session.

text.label: Microlight or paramotor flights
text.description: A flight-family option covering two distinct piloted aircraft modes. Record the whole selected flight session or refine it to one of the two modes.

text.label: Drone racing
aliases: Pilot a sport drone on a course or race
text.description: Pilot a sport drone through an obstacle course or race using a visual feed or FPV.

text.label: Helicopter sport
aliases: Pilot a helicopter in a sport event
text.description: Pilot a helicopter in a sport task, flying a route or performing maneuvers under Rotorcraft rules.

text.label: Motorcycle trials
text.description: Ride slowly through obstacle sections on a motorcycle, maintaining balance and avoiding touches or penalties.

text.label: Motorcycle rally raid
aliases: Take part in a motorcycle rally raid or cross-country event
text.description: Ride a long off-road route in a motorcycle cross-country or rally raid event, following its navigation rules.

text.label: Bandy
text.description: Play bandy on an ice field, using sticks to move a ball and score goals under bandy rules.

text.label: Rink bandy
text.description: Play rink bandy, a version of bandy on a smaller ice surface with a corresponding team size and rules.

text.label: Short bandy
text.description: Play short bandy on a shorter field under the rules of this short-format version.

text.label: Basque pelota: hand
text.description: Play without a racket, using the hand to send the pelota alternately to the front wall of a fronton or trinquet. Protective joint pads do not change the way the game is played.

text.label: Basque pelota: frontball
text.description: Play by hand on a court with one front wall, striking a rubber ball into the permitted wall area and returning it to the opponent.

text.label: Basque pelota: frontenis
text.description: Play frontenis by hitting a ball with a racket against the front wall of a fronton and returning it to the playing area under this form of pelota’s rules. Specialized balls and rackets are used.

text.label: Basque pelota: cesta punta
text.description: Catch the ball in a long, curved cesta, guide or accelerate it along the basket, and throw it at the front wall of the fronton.

text.label: Basque pelota: xare
text.description: Play with a xare ring-shaped racket strung with netting: catch or briefly hold the ball and fling it with a forearm movement rather than striking it with taut strings.

text.label: Basque pelota: leather paleta
text.description: Hit a leather pelota with a short wooden paleta toward the front wall of a fronton or trinquet.

text.label: Basque pelota: pala corta
text.description: Hit a leather pelota with a heavier, solid short wooden pala on a 36-meter fronton.

text.label: Basque pelota: rubber paleta
text.description: Hit a rubber pelota with a wooden, carbon-fiber, or fiberglass paleta on a fronton or in a trinquet.

text.label: Sumo
text.description: Wrestle in a dohyō, trying to push an opponent out of the ring or make any part of their body other than the soles of their feet touch its inner surface.

text.label: Tug of war
text.description: Pull a rope as a team in a sport competition, trying to move the opposing team beyond a designated line.

text.label: Ice stock sport
text.description: Slide and steer a special Icestock stick over a playing surface toward a target area or in relation to other sticks. The game is played on ice in winter and on an approved hard surface in summer.

text.label: Pool lifesaving
text.description: Take part in pool lifesaving by completing swimming stages, moving a mannequin, and using rescue equipment according to the discipline’s format.

text.label: Beach and ocean lifesaving
aliases: Compete in beach or ocean lifesaving
text.description: Take part in beach or ocean lifesaving events, completing running, swimming, or rescue-craft stages.

text.label: Team rescue simulation
aliases: Compete in a team SERC rescue simulation
text.description: As a team, assess a set emergency scenario and complete a sequence of rescue and first-aid actions within a time limit in a SERC competition. This is a controlled team competition, not a real-world rescue. Recording the whole event is valid; the simulated response actions need not be split out.

text.label: Rescue boat races
aliases: Race in a surf boat or IRB lifesaving event
text.description: Take part in lifesaving races in watercraft, including rowing rescue boats and inflatable motorized rescue boats.

text.label: Bridge
text.description: Play contract bridge with a partner: bid a contract and then work together to play the card tricks.

text.label: Powerboat racing
aliases: Race a powerboat on a circuit
text.description: Race a high-speed motorboat around a circuit, steering the boat and competing for speed.

text.label: Offshore racing
aliases: Compete in an offshore powerboat race
text.description: Race a motorboat over an open-water course, competing for speed or placement.

text.label: RC boats
text.description: Pilot a radio-controlled motor racing boat around a marked water course.

text.label: Jet ski racing
text.description: Race a motorized personal watercraft on the water.

text.label: MotoSurf
text.description: Ride a motor-powered MotoSurf board, performing maneuvers or runs on the water.

text.label: Artistic cycling
text.description: Perform figures, balance elements, gymnastic and choreographic sequences on an artistic cycling bike, individually, in pairs, or in a group according to the chosen format.

text.label: Artistic gymnastics
text.description: Perform gymnastics exercises and routines on one or more apparatus.

text.label: Artistic roller skating
text.description: Perform artistic and dance routines on roller skates, individually, in pairs, or in a group. The program type and composition depend on the chosen discipline.

text.label: Beach hockey
text.description: Play hockey with a ball on a sand court under Beach Hockey rules.

text.label: Beach wrestling
text.description: Wrestle standing inside a small circle on sand, trying to score with a throw or control, or force the opponent out of the circle.

text.label: Belt wrestling
text.description: Grip an opponent’s belt or clothing and use throws or holds under the rules of the selected official belt-wrestling style.

text.label: Biathlon range shooting
aliases: Shoot at a biathlon rifle range
text.description: Shoot at targets with a biathlon rifle during the event’s shooting stages. The equipment and rules are specific to biathlon.

text.label: Bodysurfing
text.description: Catch a sea wave and glide along its surface using your body, without a board.

text.label: Box lacrosse
text.description: Play a faster, contact version of lacrosse in an enclosed area, using a stick and ball under box-lacrosse rules.

text.label: Freestyle kayaking
text.description: Perform tricks, maneuvers, and held moves in a river hole or wave using a kayak or canoe, with technique and difficulty judged.

text.label: Canoe polo
text.description: Play a team ball game on the water, maneuvering in kayaks with paddles and passing or throwing the ball toward goals.

text.label: Speed climbing
text.description: Climb a standard speed-climbing route against the clock while on top-rope belay. The specific belay device depends on the venue and format.

text.label: Coastal endurance rowing
text.description: Row a coastal boat along an open-water course, rounding buoys and adapting to waves and wind. Course length and format depend on the race.

text.label: Coastal rowing
text.description: Row a rowing craft in coastal waters as part of a coastal-rowing discipline. Rowing on an ergometer and recreational boating are not included.

text.label: Pahlavani
text.description: Wrestle an opponent standing and on the ground, using throws and grips, including permitted grips around the belt and knee areas of specialized trousers under the style’s rules.

text.label: Kazakh kures
text.description: Wrestle standing in qazaq kuresi, gripping the opponent above the waist and using throws, trips, and hooks to try to put them on their back or both shoulders.

text.label: Cycle ball
text.description: Play a team ball match while riding bicycles, moving the ball with the bicycle or wheel and scoring goals.

text.label: Bike trials
text.description: Ride a bicycle over marked natural or artificial obstacles, controlling the bike and maintaining balance. Competition rules separately define how contact and section completion are scored.

text.label: Disc accuracy throw
aliases: Throw a flying disc for accuracy
text.description: Throw a flying disc at designated targets or zones to score for accuracy under the rules of the specific discipline.

text.label: Disc distance throw
aliases: Throw a flying disc for distance
text.description: Throw a flying disc as far as possible under the rules of the distance discipline; technique and measurement are set by its regulations.

text.label: Dragon boat
text.description: Paddle in synchrony as a team in a long, multi-seat boat, using single-bladed paddles in a distance race.

text.label: Carriage driving
text.description: Drive a horse or team in harness and guide the horse-drawn carriage along a chosen route or around an arena.

text.label: Endurance riding
text.description: Ride a horse over a long route, adjusting pace and monitoring the horse’s condition across changing terrain and distance.

text.label: Equestrian vaulting
